overall_comments: Strong Grade 2 time-unit lesson. ALIGNMENT=4: E2.4 named in primary_expectations, lesson activities (sort 16 event cards by unit, time real events, 60-rule discussion) directly address it; curriculum_expectations text matches input_row.json byte-for-byte; explicit Day-3 callback ('Remember Day 3: the ruler told us LENGTH in cm. Today the stopwatch tells us TIME in seconds and minutes — same idea: the right TOOL gives the right NUMBER') and Day-5 forward-bridge ('tomorrow Roo + Cal join forces — measure ALL attributes at the capstone stations'). PEDAGOGICAL_DEPTH=4: trap is grade-level-specific wrong-time-unit confusion (brushing teeth = 2 SECONDS), cited to Lehrer (2003) attribute-tool matching for time, and recovery_moves branch by diagnostic (A: physical-benchmark drill; B: predict-then-time; C: stopwatch colon-format). INSTRUCTIONAL_BALANCE=4: materials are everyday (anchor chart, event cards, stopwatch); puppets explicitly OPTIONAL ('OPTIONAL: Roo and Cal — if available; otherwise teacher voices both ... or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures'); NO-MATERIALS body-pose alternative present in differentiation ('children stand for HOURS (big stretch up), sit for MINUTES (medium pose), and clap for SECONDS (quick). Body becomes the time-unit display'); 12/25/13 = 50 min realistic for G2. CLARITY_VOICE=4: Cal anchors hook, action, and consolidation; success_criteria all 'I can'; quotable refrain 'SECONDS for the FAST, MINUTES for the MEDIUM, HOURS for the LONG!' chanted 3x at exit, plus unit close 'SMALL unit, BIG count — BIG unit, small count!'; child-friendly definitions for every vocab term in blueprint. MATHEMATICAL_AUTHENTICITY=4: conceptual progression unit-attribute-tool matching; STRATEGY COMPARE explicit in step 6 ('two pairs share HOW they ESTIMATED before timing — Pair A Mississippi-counting; Pair B body-pose method. Class debates which is closer to actual'); Lehrer (2003) named in research grounding; vocabulary precise (duration/second/minute/hour). LESSON_WORKSHEET_CONSISTENCY=4: worksheet's Part 1 (pick unit for 6 events) practises success criterion 'I can pick the right unit'; Part 2 (60s = ? min, 2h = ? min) practises '60 seconds = 1 minute'; Part 3 (3 home events) is a transfer task to home context, deliberately varying from in-class event cards — generalization is justified.
